raw_case_text:
Case-1: A 60-year-old man with non-treated arterial hypertension and overweight (BMI =28.7kg/m2) was admitted to the ICU in March 2020 for an ARDS after a "flu-like syndrome" during the preceding two weeks. After 2 weeks of at-home prednisolone (20mg/day) treatment, his clinical status deteriorated with an arterial saturation at 70% requiring an emergency medical ambulance intervention. At arrival, the medical team decided to intubate and ventilate the patient before transportation to the ICU. At ICU admission, the examination showed: moderate tachycardia (90 bpm); elevated blood pressure (170/80 mmHg); moderate hyperthermia (38.0 C); and a 120 mmHg PaO2 at FiO2 1 and PEEP 18 cmH2O. A positive PCR test for SARS-CoV-2 confirmed the COVID-19 diagnosis, highly suspected on a chest CT scan showing a major alveolo-interstitial pneumonia. The PCR tests were repeated 7 times during the ICU hospitalization, and it became negative after the day 25th post-admission. The initial transthoracic 2D Echo-Doppler revealed a diastolic dysfunction with a hypertrophied left ventricle and an altered left ventricular ejection fraction (40%). The initial treatment consisted of hydroxychloroquine (200mg), ceftriaxone (2g), and azithromycin (500mg). The microbiological evaluation (pharyngeal swab) was positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae treated by cefepime for 8 days. Despite prone positioning and inhaled NO (10ppm; Inomax DS IR, Linde) the persistent severe hypoxia led to making the decision to start (day 4) a veno-venous ECMO assistance. Under methylprednisolone treatment (50mg q4 during 15 days), a distal lung-protected sampling at day 2 (+22 days after initial symptoms; 6th day post-ICU admission) was positive Enterobacter aerogenes was treated by meropenem (2g q3), and rapidly replaced by piperacillin after testing the sensitivity.
The improvement in lung function allowed us to wean the patient from the VV-ECMO after 11 days. On day 26 post ICU admission, bronchopneumonia was diagnosed with new images on the chest X-ray and gas exchange alteration. The distal lung-protected sampling was positive for wild-type Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterobacter aerogenes carrying a cephalosporinase, treated by piperacillin-tazobactam 4g q4, rapidly shifted after sensitivity testing to aerosols of colimycine, meropenem, and amikacine. The detected reactivation of CMV particles (RT-PCR) both in the lung and blood motivated to give ganciclovir for 2 weeks (10mg/kg/day). On the day 25 post-admission (32 days post symptoms) the laboratory exams showed a persistent absolute lymphopenia at 0.21G/L with a monocytopenia at 0.08 G/L, and a moderate pleocytosis (PMNs) with elevated ferritin (1238 ng/mL), LDH (250 UI/L), long-lasting positive SARS-Cov-2 PCR and severe clinical alteration. New investigations were then performed: - the myelogram that eliminated a macrophage activation syndrome; the repeated measurement of peripheral blood monocyte HLA-DR expression (flowcytometer FACSCanto II, Becton Dickinson, as previously reported). The first mHLA-DR (day 24 after ICU admission) expression value was dramatically low (1760 AB/C), largely lower than the threshold diagnostic level of 8000 AB/C for AIDS. The diagnosis of AIDs associated with recurrent secondary infections, poor clinical status, and low absolute count of peripheral lymphocytes, motivated the decision to treat this AIDs at day 28 post-admission (day 42 post symptoms) with subcutaneous IFNgamma (100mcg per injection; Immukin, Boerhinger, Germany), as previously reported. The IFNgamma was chosen for several reasons: it has been tested safely many years ago and it is largely used for several immune diseases; it was shown efficient in severe ICU patients with AIDs or severe fungal infections; - COVID-19 was shown to have a deficit in IFNgamma release (9 16). After the agreement of the relatives for compassionate use, IFNgamma was given at 100mcg per day subcutaneously for 7 days. Expression mHLA-DRwas monitored by flowcytometry monitoring every 3 days.  Figure 1  shows the evolution of mHLA DR expression, lymphocyte absolute number having a peak at day 3 after IFNgamma initiation. After stopping the drug administration, the mHLA-DR expression remained above the threshold of AIDs with no concomitant change in the absolute number of lymphocytes. As previously reported, lymphopenia improved after a long delay. The week after starting IFNgamma treatment, the clinical status improved with no occurrence of a new secondary infection, allowing to wean the patient from mechanical ventilation. He was finally discharged from the ICU at day 54 after admission (68 days after initial symptoms).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 60-year-old man presented with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and severe hypoxemia following a 2-week flu-like syndrome.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In March 2020, the patient experienced a 2-week flu-like illness treated at home with oral prednisolone (20 mg/day) before acutely deteriorating with an arterial oxygen saturation of 70%, requiring pre-hospital endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and emergency transfer to the ICU.
subjective.past_medical_history: Untreated arterial hypertension and overweight (BMI 28.7 kg/m2).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 2-week flu-like illness and severe dyspnea/hypoxemia. Pre-admission medication: oral prednisolone 20 mg/day for 2 weeks.

objective.physical_examination: At ICU admission (intubated and mechanically ventilated): heart rate 90 bpm (moderate tachycardia), blood pressure 170/80 mmHg, temperature 38.0 °C, pre-intubation SpO2 70%.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission ABG: PaO2 120 mmHg on FiO2 1.0 and PEEP 18 cmH2O. Transthoracic 2D Echo-Doppler showed left ventricular hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, and reduced LVEF of 40%. Nasopharyngeal SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR positive on admission (remained positive across 7 tests until turning negative after ICU day 25). Pharyngeal swab positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae. ICU day 26 chest X-ray showed new bronchopneumonia infiltrates. ICU day 25 labs: persistent absolute lymphopenia (0.21 G/L), monocytopenia (0.08 G/L), moderate polymorphonuclear pleocytosis, elevated ferritin (1,238 ng/mL), and LDH (250 UI/L).
objective.advanced_workup: Admission chest CT showed major alveolo-interstitial pneumonia. Protected distal lung sampling on ICU day 6 grew Enterobacter aerogenes, and on ICU day 26 grew wild-type Pseudomonas aeruginosa and cephalosporinase-producing Enterobacter aerogenes alongside positive CMV RT-PCR in both lung and blood. Bone marrow myelogram ruled out macrophage activation syndrome. Flow cytometry (FACSCanto II) on ICU day 24 demonstrated severely depressed monocyte HLA-DR (mHLA-DR) expression at 1,760 AB/C (diagnostic threshold for acquired immunodeficiency <8,000 AB/C).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with severe COVID-19 ARDS complicated by secondary bacterial ventilator-associated bronchopneumonias (Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterobacter aerogenes, Pseudomonas aeruginosa), pulmonary and viremic cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation (confirmed by positive CMV RT-PCR in lung and blood), and severe ICU-acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (confirmed by mHLA-DR 1,760 AB/C and profound lymphopenia 0.21 G/L). Managed with veno-venous ECMO (ICU days 4 to 15), methylprednisolone (50 mg q4h for 15 days), targeted antibiotics (cefepime, meropenem, piperacillin-tazobactam, and nebulized colistin/meropenem/amikacin), intravenous ganciclovir (10 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks) for CMV reactivation, and compassionate-use subcutaneous interferon-gamma (IFN-gamma 100 mcg/day for 7 days starting ICU day 28). Monocyte HLA-DR expression recovered above 8,000 AB/C with lymphocyte peak on day 3 of IFN-gamma, enabling weaning from mechanical ventilation and ICU discharge on day 54 (day 68 post-symptom onset).
